title: JEPA World Models: From Prediction to Decisions
summary: An evidence-led tutorial that tests when predictive representations help action selection—and when accurate prediction is not enough.
description: This research tutorial connects JEPA representation learning, action-conditioned prediction, planning, uncertainty, and decision evaluation. It includes small local LeJEPA objective studies, a verified inference check with an official V-JEPA 2.1 checkpoint, and clearly labeled MountainCar analogues. Notebook 23 adds a preregistered 660-episode visual study; its decision result remains partial because all five JEPA seeds triggered a low-spread diagnostic. Toy results are not presented as paper reproductions. A genuine learned-JEPA-versus-direct-policy benchmark remains future work.

status.label: Active research tutorial
status.summary: Local lessons and evidence are available. Notebook 22 and the preregistered Notebook 23 matrix are complete. Notebook 23's JEPA outcomes remain exploratory because all five fits triggered low spread; a learned-JEPA-versus-direct-policy comparison and large paper benchmarks remain future work.

researchQuestion: When do predictive representations actually improve action selection, and when does accurate prediction fail to translate into effective decisions?

verifiedFindings.title: Small local objective studies produced mixed probe results
verifiedFindings.summary: On a five-seed CIFAR-10 subset, the SIGReg frozen-probe difference was -0.24 points (95% interval [-1.591, 1.111], including zero). In a separate five-seed study, RDMReg improved the local projector probe by 6.94 points over a weak teaching proxy, while the encoder-probe difference was 0.06 points.
verifiedFindings.scope: Two local CIFAR-10 subset studies with small CNNs; five seeds per study.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Neither result is the corresponding ImageNet paper benchmark. The RDMReg result is sensitive to a degenerate teaching proxy.

verifiedFindings.title: Near-perfect action ranking did not make local MPC successful
verifiedFindings.summary: The state model ranked 60/60 non-tied action pairs correctly, yet MPC reached 0/20 goals and a direct momentum rule reached 20/20. The planner used 7.68 million model transitions and 12.747 seconds; the rule used no model transitions and 0.007 seconds.
verifiedFindings.scope: One deterministic polynomial Ridge model; MountainCarContinuous; 20 paired starts.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Not a JEPA result or matched-actual-compute comparison. It applies only to the recorded local task and settings.

verifiedFindings.title: A hand-written controller prior changed CEM outcomes
verifiedFindings.summary: On 20 paired starts, neutral-start CEM reached 0/20 goals; momentum-prior CEM and direct control each reached 20/20. Direct control used zero model calls and averaged fewer steps than the prior planner.
verifiedFindings.scope: One fixed color-moment feature extractor and one Ridge fit on rendered MountainCar frames.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: The prior is hand-written, not a learned policy. This is not PiJEPA or a learned JEPA planner.

verifiedFindings.title: Planner-shift coverage intervals were wider across five fits
verifiedFindings.summary: For 90% prediction intervals, mean position coverage was 90.7% [89.7%, 91.7%] on random actions and 89.0% [82.2%, 95.7%] under planner shift.
verifiedFindings.scope: Five independent state-space Ridge ensembles on MountainCarContinuous.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Not a JEPA uncertainty result; five fits and one task do not establish general calibration.

verifiedFindings.title: Visual JEPA outcomes depended on protocol and representation diagnostics
verifiedFindings.summary: Notebook 22 ranked 153/295 non-tied action pairs correctly; uniform-start JEPA CEM succeeded on 0/100 starts and momentum-prior CEM on 100/100, while direct control reached 20/20. In separate Notebook 23 v1, JEPA ranked 131/225 pairs correctly but succeeded on 0/100 starts with either initialization; all five JEPA fits triggered low spread. The direct controller reached 20/20, and the exact oracle reached 0/20 without the momentum prior and 20/20 with it.
verifiedFindings.scope: Two separate synthetic MountainCar studies. Notebook 22 used five learned model seeds; v1 used five paired model/data seeds and 20 shared evaluation starts.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: The studies use different objectives and protocols. All v1 JEPA fits triggered low spread, and v1 omitted prior-only CEM and a learned direct policy. These results do not establish a JEPA decision advantage or a general result, and are not paper reproductions.

pendingWork.title: Matched learned-JEPA versus direct-policy benchmark
pendingWork.summary: Compare oracle dynamics, learned state dynamics, learned visual latent dynamics, action-conditioned JEPA dynamics, direct policy, and policy-guided planning on one preregistered task with paired starts, shared data, compute accounting, and independent regeneration.
pendingWork.claimBoundary: Notebook 22 is a synthetic MountainCar analogue with a hand-written visual prior. It does not satisfy this benchmark or establish a general JEPA advantage.

pendingWork.title: Evaluate physical-state grounding in a released JEPA checkpoint
pendingWork.summary: Assess latent probes, planning, and policy outcomes for PSG-JEPA using a verified task setup and its released LIBERO-Goal checkpoint.
pendingWork.claimBoundary: The public release lists one training seed while the paper reports three-seed results. Check code, dataset, base-model, simulator, and checkpoint terms; a single checkpoint evaluation cannot reproduce the paper mean.
